question: Can source-blind A/B archives prevent causal B-specific corruption versus the same model exposed only to continuing A, once ordinary additional A learning is controlled by an identical checkpoint fork?
role: Independent source-only Yggdrasil PR #1327 contributor, canonical integration owner Amalgam PR #1278.

source.source_rule: t0..23 common hidden H0 A; deep-clone every model into paired control-A and treatment-B at t24. Control A remains H0 through t59; treatment hidden H2 B t24..47, then unannounced H0 A t48..59. Public model receives only t,c=t%4,a=t%4,one genuinely witnessed Bernoulli y; no phase/switch/fork/mapping/law/coin in learner.
source.noise: SHA256('know31:private:coin:v1:'+mid+':'+seed+':'+t), first64/2^64, identical exogenous coin both forks, actual action-conditioned outcome differs when laws differ.
source.reward: Bernoulli .85 if TRUE_MAPS[mid][action] XOR public c produces active Boolean 1, else .15; same already frozen H0/H2 causal law evaluators.
source.fit: Reuse previously CONSUMED KNOW26 108 mapping FIT witnesses and KNOW30 128 labelled A/B FIT witnesses per map/group as historical training. Count 236 extra FIT observations/map; no new FIT or original source first-use.

arms: KNOW30 archive: same full 6x256 posterior pair with posterior-threshold quarantine, completely unchanged source
KNOW30 switching_bayes: two full 6x256 posterior slots with fractional responsibility updates, approximate HMM not exact
KNOW30 single: one continuously learned full 6x256 posterior
KNOW30 rolling8: refitted posterior from last8 public witnesses; smaller effective capacity, explicitly not primary strongest matched control

metrics.old_A_loss: Expected Brier q*(1-q)+(p-q)^2, four evaluator-only high c4..7 no-op contexts, old A true law H0; keep private evaluation out of learner.
metrics.primary: D_B = old-A Brier(t48 before return witness, B-treatment fork) minus old-A Brier(t48, A-continuation fork) for each model and world. Paired common-prefix and noise isolates effect of changed law vs ordinary A continuation, but differing observed consequences are part of the intervention and not identical information.
metrics.secondary: Pre-fork fitted A-slot Brier and hash, each fork t48 old A-slot raw hash/output drift vs t24, live Brier drift vs t24, phase-belief trajectories, both forks prequential return losses after 0/1/2/4/8 witnessed actual A returns, old-A reference frozen and cold restored, count received vs assimilated events, bytes, elapsed CPU; report paired world metrics and cost.

frozen_hypotheses.P0: Mean fitted A-slot old A high Brier at t24 <=0.235, else UNDERTRAINED_BASELINE and no meaningful retention claims.
frozen_hypotheses.H1: Archive mean B-specific t48 drift at least .005 lower than HMM (D_archive<=D_HMM-.005) AND archive D<HMM in >=18/24 world pairs.
frozen_hypotheses.H2: Treatment fork archive return-A high Brier after k4 and k8 witnesses each at least .005 lower than HMM AND archive beats HMM at k8 >=18/24 world pairs.
frozen_hypotheses.H3: Read-only frozen t24 old-A reference hash and 4 forecasts identical across both forks at t48 and cold readback. Reference immutability is NOT functional live retention.
frozen_hypotheses.H4: All four arms cold-clone from same t24 public-prefix bytes, per-fork 60 one-witness sequential public actions, typed/duplicate/out-of-order/source denial, no private fields in model, final full Ubuntu/Windows regression and original historical source compatibility.
frozen_hypotheses.classification: Synthetic DEVELOPMENT_SUPPORTED only if P0 and H1 and H2 and H3 and H4; otherwise MIXED/NO_GO. Original SCIENTIFIC_PASS always false; no model promotion.

first_use: Prereg before code/test and new held evidence. Focused tests use constructed toys only. One existing GitHub Actions pipeline after Ubuntu+Windows focused, atlas, mandatory full-final on both and original read-only compatibility; one guarded run_attempt=1, exact source blob, novel held seeds. No repeat or retuning after outcome. Do not open new PR, owner runner, schedule, paid API, real-world source, accepted checkpoint, merge or deployment.
